prompt: Produce exactly one concise caption (one sentence) that states only visually verifiable facts. Include 2–6 discrete visual facts drawn from this checklist in the given priority order when present: 1) legible text: transcribe exact words; 2) counts and object types (e.g., "2 people", "one bicycle"); 3) key color/material/texture for those objects (e.g., "orange backpack", "wooden façade"); 4) pose/action/orientation (e.g., "person seen from behind walking away; holding two poles"); 5) simple spatial layout (foreground / midground / background placement); 6) lighting/viewpoint/occlusion cues (e.g., "bright sunlight casting long shadows", "elevated vantage; tree partially obscures façade"). Use canonical object names and exact counts, standard direction words (left/right/foreground/background), and numerals or short words for numbers. Do not infer roles, emotions, intentions, or use metaphors, slogans, or marketing language (avoid "farmer", "happy", "adventure", etc.). If text is not clearly legible, omit it rather than guess. Keep the caption factual, compact, and limited to one sentence containing 2–6 concrete facts—no lists, tags, extra sentences, or commentary. Example (good): "Sign reads 'Outdoor World'; two adults walk toward the store entrance; timber façade and concrete forecourt; overcast sky." Counterexample (bad): "A happy farmer enjoys a sunny day in the countryside."
